Elon Musk on the future of a spacefaring civilization.

Musk says the future could look like Robert Heinlein's The Moon Is a Harsh Mistress, with lunar mass drivers, computers on the Moon, and humanity expanding into deep space.

He also says anyone at SpaceX who wants to go to the Moon or Mars will eventually have that opportunity.
"Your word?" - "You have my word." 

Musk imagines a future where people live across the Solar System, eventually reaching other star systems.

"An incredibly exciting future" where humanity becomes a true spacefaring civilization.

Video

Elon Musk on the future of Star Mind. 

Musk says the Star Mind factory will be located right next to SpaceX.
But his bigger prediction is about SpaceX's future value.

He believes that within 4–5 years, Star Mind could represent 99% of SpaceX's value.

And he expects SpaceX itself to be worth an "astronomical number" by then.

If that happens, SpaceX could evolve from a space company into a massive AI and compute powerhouse.

Two years ago, Leave Delaware started with a simple idea: American companies should not treat one state’s legal system as an unquestioned default.

Since then, the conversation has changed dramatically.

Major public companies have left Delaware. Texas and Nevada have become serious competitors for corporate domiciles. Delaware has rewritten significant parts of its corporate law. Founders, boards, investors, lawyers and policymakers are now openly debating questions that were barely asked a few years ago.

Corporate law determines who controls companies, how boards make decisions, how founders are treated, how shareholders can sue, how much litigation costs, and how confidently businesses can invest for the long term. Those rules shape where capital goes, where companies grow and, ultimately, how competitive the United States remains.

Competition between states is healthy. No jurisdiction should be entitled to permanent dominance simply because “that’s how it has always been done.”

We’re grateful to everyone who has followed, shared, argued with, challenged and contributed to this effort. The next phase can be much bigger, and we want more people involved.

We’re looking for exceptional people who can help with social media, original content, data, legal research, white papers and deeper analysis.

We’re also looking for people willing to fund the work. Serious research, distribution and advocacy require resources. If you believe corporate-law competition matters, we want to hear from you.

And the easiest way to help costs nothing: follow @leavedelaware and share our work. Every founder, investor, lawyer and policymaker who sees this debate makes the market for corporate law more competitive.

If you have talent, capital or reach and want to help build the next phase of Leave Delaware, DM us.

We’re still early.

.@elonmusk on why AI should care about humanity. 

"It’s important that we have an AI that cares about humanity, fosters humanity, and helps take us to other planets and other star systems."

Musk says this is why SpaceX needs to succeed in both AI hardware and software.

He believes an AI built by SpaceX would inherit the capabilities and values of the people building it.

"SpaceX is a collection of some of the very best humans on Earth."

For Musk, the goal isn't just to build smarter AI.

It's to build AI that helps humanity survive, explore, and become a multiplanetary civilization.
